name: MINER self-transfer credits the pair twice
summary: MINER (an ERC20/ERC1155 hybrid named ERC_X) caches both balances in _update and writes _balances[to] = toBalance + value after debiting _balances[from], so a transfer with from == to credits value out of nothing. The attacker flash-borrowed 10 WBNB from DODO, bought 0.00001 MINER, sent it to the MINER/WBNB pair and called skim(pair) 50 times; each skim self-transferred the pair's excess and doubled it, and swap() then took the pair's 3.5 WBNB against the inflated MINER balance.
notes: The defect is the self-transfer double credit in ERC_X._update, not a transfer fee: MINER has none, and the anchor's pair-to-pair Transfer logs double from 0.00001 MINER each loop. The pair is the victim, not a target.

Reset: deployment. The deployer's addLiquidityETH (0xc8a9cda0, 38 blocks later) flipped easyLaunch (slot 0xb) and whitelisted the pair, which only skips the NFT mint and burn; the double credit does not depend on it. The pair's only other transactions before the anchor and in the 90 days after are two 10-MINER buys (by the deployer and 0xc41bf661); campaign.mjs found no other outflow.

Loss is the pair's whole WBNB reserve, the 3.5 BNB the deployer 0x06f8fc2c added; the deployer is a serial launcher that added and removed 3.5 BNB of liquidity on many short-lived tokens, and the attacker 0x031958a8, funded through 0xd47438c8, has no visible link to it.
